raw_recipe.headline: Cajun Seasoning Spice Mix
raw_recipe.description: This easy Cajun seasoning mix can be made at home with common spices from your pantry including paprika, garlic powder, thyme, and cayenne pepper.

video.description: This is a mildly hot Cajun spice mix you make yourself with common spices from your pantry. For those who like it hotter, add the optional crushed red pepper. Use this spice mix to make great Cajun hash browns in the oven!
video.name: DIY Cajun Seasoning

raw_recipe.name: Cajun Seasoning Spice Mix

review.reviewBody: This made great cajun spice. I used this to make cajun-mayo for cajun spiced burgers and made some cajun shrimp. I only used half the salt. I used the crushed red pepper flakes and we didn't consider this too hot at all. This made enough for both dishes and there is plenty left for a couple more dishes. Thanks for sharing Diamondlil, this is better than the store bought blends and I can control the salt!

this cajun spice is great! i used 1 tsp of salt instead of 2. i've made thisa few times now, its easy to mixup the ingredients with different spices i just keep the recipe amount of garlic powder, black pepper, onion powder, cayenne and red pepper flakes. it's great on potatoes, eggs, popcorn and tofu! i will always keep this spice mix of some variation on hand!

I thought that this was a solid recipe. I'm wondering though if the people who claim that it was far too salty were using table salt instead of kosher salt. I started with half the salt and found it a little bland. So I actually added a teaspoon of MSG instead of salt. And that seemed just about perfect to me. I did not add the pepper flakes. I thought the heat level was good and did not need to be increased. One thing that I did find initially was that the thyme just felt like little sticks in my mouth so I put the whole thing in my spice grinder for 10 or 15 seconds. That seemed to take care of the thyme problem and mixed everything up very well.

This is a great mix to keep on hand. I used it tonight for my mahi mahi fish and the taste was phenomenal. The only thing I added was a tsp of smoked paprika to give it a bigger kick. Hubby loved it! Made extra to store for the next time. I’m gonna try it on chicken breast and I’m sure it’ll be just as delicious?
Daughter made it for me, added a dash "1/4 teaspoon" of brown sugar for an offset sweet and spicy! Little one sure can cook!!! Made Cajun burgers and noodle casserole. Thanks for the recipe!

I adore this, I’ve used it on chicken and pork and it’s really really good. The flavours are amazing! Regarding the paprika-after I’d used a teaspoon, I’d run out so the remaining 1.5tsp was smoked paprika so this is how I always make it now. Also- I’m not sure if it’s just me but I found that 3/4 tsp of salt was more than enough. For anyone using this recipe for the first time, I’d half the salt and adjust next time :)

I am so grateful for this wonderful site and rarely write a review. This time, I felt compelled. I found this recipe to be far too salty! Though I do use salt regularly to season my food, this was so salty that I nearly had to throw it away. If you are a heavy salt user, I suspect you will not notice; but for the rest, I suggest you cut the salt by at least?? half.
Great recipe! We don't like a lot of oregano, so I used 1 tsp basil and 1/4 tsp oregano. Gave my Jambalaya the zing it needed!

Have used in my gumbo for years & keep on hand as a rub. Store bought varieties tend to add sugars or additives unnecessarily. We cut the salt for heart health and love that we can dial up or down the heat with the pepper flakes depending on what we're making and who we're making it for. Thanks for years of flavour!

I omit the salt entirely. I'm trying to reduce salt in my diet and had to stop buying Cajun seasoning because it's so full of salt! With homemade, I can control my sodium and still enjoy the flavor! I use this in Red Beans and Rice, jambalaya, on popcorn and corn on the cob!
This was good but not quite as hot or spicy as I prefer so the 2nd time I increased the cayenne and added cumin. That made it just right for me.

This recipe took me back to when I was stationed at Fort Polk in the ER as a Medical Corpsman/Ambulance Driver, and that was like in the last century! This recipe is as close to anything I have tried to make before! What I mean is this recipe was the star of the Cajun Chicken with Pasta! It was just awesome! And if you ask my wife, she will tell you that I will put it on anything, Breakfast, Lunch or Dinner!

I love this recipe - you saved the day! I was in France, and it's kind of a novelty to find Cajun (or Creole) spices, and of course I didn't find any at the local supermarket. I used my phone to look up your recipe, and was able to make a terrific chicken and sausage jambalaya for my family. I toned it down as some people are a bit older and can't handle too much spiciness. But it was quite good and really was delicious. Big thanks from the old country!
Great. Did not use salt.
Very easy to make and use. I added it to alfredo sauce and it came out great. Added a little extra cayenne because I like a bit more of a kick.

**Edit: Coming back here four years later to say that I still make and use this recipe. I multiply the amount and keep a jar in my cabinet. When I’m out, I make it again. Still use it for the sausage, green bean, potato dish, but it also goes well with shrimp, pork, and roasted potatoes. One of my essential recipes! Thanks for sharing. I made this recipe as written, opting not to use the red pepper flakes and felt it had the right amount of heat. I wanted to try making the recipe "Instant Pot sausage, green beans, and potatoes" and it called for cajun spice mix, but I didn't have any. I'm grateful I found this because I had everything in my pantry. I will triple it next time and keep the mix handy for next time I make the IP sausage dish (google it) because it was fantastic, quick and easy!
This was delicious! I used it in the recipe "VooDoo Pasta" on this site. Yum!
So grateful this was posted! Perfect balance of herbs and spices for a solid cajun spice mix.

I have been using this as my "go-too" spice mix for just about everything. My only complaint is that the recipe doesn't have a built-in computer in order to make bigger batches more easily. I make it a couple of cups at a time. It keeps indefinitely as long it is in a tight sealing glass jar with a dark storage location.
I would reduce the salt a bit as one of us is salt restricted.
